name: Respond to producer tenders
summary: Oil and gas producers buy fracturing programs and annual cementing and coiled tubing work through tenders, and the company has a few weeks to answer each one with a technical proposal and a priced schedule of hundreds of line items. An account manager leads the bid, a technical sales engineer estimates the stages, horsepower, fluids and sand, a pricing analyst fills in the schedule from the price book and supplier quotes, and the vice president of sales approves the price. Bids are slow because sand, trucking and fuel quotes, clarification answers and approvals all sit in queues, and error-prone because quantities and line items are copied by hand between the producer's workbook, the price book and the margin model.

baseline.org_archetype: A listed Canadian pressure pumper of about 1,350 people serving 60-plus producers in Alberta and northeast BC, with a 20-person Calgary sales team.
baseline.notes: Covers both fracturing program tenders (larger, about a third of cases) and annual cementing and coiled tubing tenders; the step times are weighted toward the frac tenders. Ends at award or loss notice.

trigger: A producer issues a tender or request for quotation for a fracturing program or annual cementing or coiled tubing work.
end_state: The bid is declined, or submitted and the producer's award or regret notice is recorded and, if won, handed over to agreement and program planning.

volume.seasonality: Most annual and program tenders are issued from September to December for the next year's budget, with pad-by-pad tenders through the year.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate: more than 60 customers, most programs rebid yearly or per pad.

surge.cause: Autumn budget season when producers tender the next year's completion programs and annual service contracts

evidence.note: Firm commitments for the next year's fleets were secured in the autumn (worldoil-2018, November 2018); multiplier tier C.
Account managers lead each bid: intake, go/no-go, questions, price review, handover; about 7 hours per tender.
Pricing schedule, cost model, supplier quotes and re-pricing take about 15 hours per tender; four analysts also maintain the price book.
Scope and quantity estimate of about 8 hours per tender.
Bid register, prequalification check, exceptions, assembly and upload; about 7 hours per tender.
Two approvals per tender plus repricing loops.
Reviews non-standard terms on about a quarter of bids.
Confirms fleet availability; not listed for this process in the organisation file.
Updates prequalification records when a bid finds them out of date; not listed for this process in the organisation file.

systems.name: Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
Business intelligence dashboards on ERP and job data
HSE incident, hazard assessment and audit system
Fracture and cement placement modelling software
Dispatch and crew scheduling board (scheduling module, whiteboards, spreadsheets)
ERP (finance, procurement, inventory, plant maintenance, billing)

steps.name: Receive tender invitation
steps.description: The account manager gets an invitation from the producer's sourcing portal or by email for a fracturing program, or an annual cementing or coiled tubing call for bids. They open the package, note the due date, the wells or pads covered and the program window, and forward it to the contract administrator.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Log tender in bid register
steps.description: The contract administrator downloads every file from the portal (instructions, pricing schedule, well list, draft contract terms), saves them to the bid folder and adds a line to the bid register with the customer, scope, deadline, question deadline and owner.

error.defect_description: Wrong deadline or a missed addendum logged.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Decide whether to bid
steps.description: The account manager compares the scope with the account plan, the fleet calendar and the customer's payment record and recent pricing. They write a short bid or no-bid note with the expected margin, the competitors likely to bid and whether crews are free in the program window.

next.condition: no fleet capacity, poor margin or poor payer

evidence.note: Price competition and customers switching suppliers described in worldoil-2018; bid or no-bid share is a tier C estimate.

steps.name: Approve bid strategy
steps.description: The vice president of sales reads the bid note, sets the pricing stance (hold price, discount to win, or price for margin) and confirms whether the company will commit a fleet. Approval is given by email or in the weekly sales meeting.

control.basis: Sales delegation of authority: VP sales approves every tender pursuit and price stance

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Check prequalification and insurance status
steps.description: The contract administrator logs in to the producer's prequalification portal and checks the company's grade, the safety statistics on file and whether the insurance certificate and limits meet the tender. Gaps are listed for the HSE team.

control.basis: Producer contractor prequalification requirement (for example an ISNetworld PASS grade) before award

next.condition: grade, statistics or certificate out of date

evidence.note: Producers require ISNetworld qualification before work (ovintiv-suppliers, cnrl-suppliers). Gap rate tier C.

steps.name: Update prequalification records
steps.description: The HSE data coordinator uploads the latest safety statistics, programs and insurance certificate to the portal and answers the reviewer's questions so the grade returns to passing before the bid is evaluated.

evidence.note: Supplier maintains a passing ISNetworld grade (ovintiv-suppliers). Times tier C.

steps.name: Submit clarification questions
steps.description: The account manager collects questions from engineering and pricing (water source, sand specification, who supplies sand and fuel, standby terms, pad access) and posts them on the portal before the question deadline.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Wait for producer answers
steps.description: The producer's supply chain team consolidates questions from all bidders and issues an addendum or answer sheet on the portal. Work on scope continues in parallel, but price assumptions stay open until the answers arrive.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Build technical scope
steps.description: The technical sales engineer reads the well list and offset data, estimates stages per well, fluid system, pump rate, horsepower, proppant and fluid volumes, and runs a design case in the modelling software. The result is the quantity sheet that drives the price.

error.defect_description: Volumes, stage count or horsepower mis-estimated, so the price misses cost.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times. The org file lists te-frac-treatment-design and te-technical-sales-support as inputs.

steps.name: Confirm fleet and crew availability
steps.description: The fracturing operations manager checks the fleet calendar for the program window, the crews that will be staffed then and any equipment in the shop, and confirms which fleet would do the work or that the dates cannot be met.

evidence.note: Crew staffing limits and fleets booked through the quarter (step-2021). Times tier C.

steps.name: Request sand, trucking and fuel quotes
steps.description: The pricing analyst emails sand suppliers, trucking carriers and the fuel supplier for delivered prices to the pad location for the tendered volume and window, unless the producer supplies its own sand.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Wait for supplier quotes
steps.description: Sand suppliers and carriers return delivered prices by email, often with validity limited to the quarter and with fuel surcharges that change monthly. The analyst chases late replies by phone.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Fill in the producer's pricing schedule
steps.description: The pricing analyst copies the producer's line items (horsepower per hour or per stage, chemicals per litre, proppant per tonne, trucking, standby, mobilisation) into the bid workbook, looks up each item in the price book, applies the discount set in the strategy and adds pass-through costs.

error.defect_description: Line item missed, unit of measure mismatched or price book rate copied wrong.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Run job cost and margin model
steps.description: The analyst prices the job from the cost side (pump hours and repair cost per hour, crew cost, sand and trucking, fuel, chemicals) and compares the bid revenue per well with cost to show margin per well and per fleet day.

error.defect_description: Cost rate out of date for inflation in fuel, sand or wages.

evidence.note: Labour and input cost inflation that bids had to pass on (step-2021). Times tier C.

steps.name: Review terms and draft exceptions
steps.description: The contract administrator compares the tender's contract terms with the company's existing MSA with that producer and standard positions, and drafts a list of exceptions (indemnities, payment terms, price adjustment, standby).

next.condition: standard terms or existing MSA applies

evidence.note: Clauses that drive negotiation in oilfield MSAs (bj-msa). Share needing legal tier C.

steps.name: Review price against market
steps.description: The account manager compares the price per stage and per well with the last award, known competitor pricing and the customer's expectations, and sends the workbook back with changes when it is out of line.

evidence.note: Commoditised pricing and customer switching (worldoil-2018). Rework share tier C.

steps.name: Legal review of tender terms
steps.description: Legal counsel reads the non-standard clauses flagged by the contract administrator, judges which are acceptable and words the exceptions that go with the bid.

evidence.note: Indemnity and insurance clauses in oilfield service contracts (bj-msa, ablawg-k4k). Times tier C.

steps.name: Approve final price
steps.description: The vice president of sales reviews the price summary, margin per fleet day and exceptions and signs off, or sends it back for a lower or higher price.

control.basis: Sales delegation of authority: price approval below standard margin

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Assemble the bid package
steps.description: The contract administrator puts together the technical proposal, completed pricing schedule, exceptions, safety statistics, equipment list and signed bid forms in the order the tender requires, and checks every requested document is present.

error.defect_description: A required form or attachment left out.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Check package against instructions
steps.description: The account manager reads the package against the tender checklist, looks at the price summary once more and confirms the technical proposal matches the quantities priced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Upload bid to the portal
steps.description: The contract administrator uploads each file to the producer's portal, fills in the online price fields where the portal asks for them separately, submits before the deadline and saves the confirmation.

error.defect_description: Online price fields do not match the attached schedule.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Wait for evaluation
steps.description: The producer's supply chain and completions teams compare bids on price per well, fleet quality, safety record and past performance. Some come back with questions or a request for best and final pricing.

evidence.note: Producers commit fleets for the next year's work programs ahead of time (worldoil-2018). Evaluation time tier C.

steps.name: Prepare best and final offer
steps.description: The pricing analyst re-runs the margin model at lower price points, the account manager agrees a floor, and the revised schedule goes back through price approval and upload.

error.defect_description: Revised schedule not matched to quantities.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Record award or loss
steps.description: The account manager receives the award letter or the regret notice, updates the bid register and CRM notes, and tells the operations and pricing teams the result.

evidence.note: Win rate about 40% is an estimate for the largest Canadian pumper with several strong competitors (worldoil-2018 describes customer switching).

steps.name: Hand over the award
steps.description: The account manager writes a short handover note with the awarded wells, dates, price basis and exceptions accepted, and sends it with the award to the contract administrator for the MSA and pricing schedule and to fracturing program planning.

error.defect_description: Exceptions or price basis not carried into the handover.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Debrief the loss
steps.description: The account manager asks the producer for feedback on where the bid ranked and why, records the winning price level if disclosed, and notes lessons in the bid register for the next round.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

exceptions.name: Prequalification lapsed
exceptions.description: The producer's portal shows an out-of-date grade or insurance certificate, which must be fixed before evaluation.

exceptions.name: Repricing loop
exceptions.description: The account manager or the vice president sends the schedule back because the price per well is out of line with the market or margin floor.

exceptions.name: Best and final round
exceptions.description: The producer asks the shortlisted bidders to sharpen their price, which repeats approval and upload.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from tender invitation to award or regret notice
benchmarks.population: Fracturing program and annual service tenders at a Canadian pressure pumper, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Estimate: tenders usually allow two to four weeks to respond and producers take two to six weeks to evaluate and award.
Estimate for a market leader facing several competitors on price (worldoil-2018 describes customer switching).

pain_points.description: Line items, units and prices are re-keyed between the producer's schedule, the price book and the margin workbook, causing repricing loops.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

pain_points.description: Sand, trucking and fuel quotes have short validity and arrive late, holding up the price while input costs rose in 2021-2022.

evidence.note: Cost inflation passed on in price increases (step-2021).

pain_points.description: Approvals wait on a single vice president who also handles customers.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a Canadian pressure pumper bidding producer tenders in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

sources.title: Master Service Agreements in the Oilfield Services Industry
sources.publisher: Bennett Jones LLP (K. Iatridis and G. Stenger)
sources.supports: MSA negotiations in oilfield services usually turn on warranties and remedies, liability and indemnification, intellectual property, insurance, and health and safety; PSAC published a template MSA and handbook of model clauses in 2017.

sources.title: Alberta Decision on Knock-for-Knock Allocation of Liability in a Standard Form Drilling Contract
sources.publisher: ABlawg (Nigel Bankes), University of Calgary Faculty of Law
sources.supports: Knock-for-knock (each party bears its own losses regardless of fault) in the CAPP/CAODC standard form; Alberta court enforced it between sophisticated parties.

sources.title: Canadian fracer rivalry heating up amid plunging share prices
sources.supports: Canadian fracturing is a commoditised, price-competitive business; customers switched between Trican and STEP; STEP secured firm commitments for over half its fleets for 2019 ahead of the year, some tied to producers' work programs.

sources.title: STEP Energy Services Ltd. Reports Fourth Quarter and Year End 2021 Results
sources.supports: Tight supply of field staff, limits on how fast recruits can be added safely, rising labour cost; prices raised for all clients in Q4 2021 and Q1 2022 to offset inflation; crews booked through Q1; spring break-up affects Canadian operations; extreme cold caused delays.

sources.title: Supplier Resources
sources.supports: A producer requires an ISNetworld PASS grade for field suppliers, a company sponsor before an agreement is set up, master agreements that mostly do not expire but are amended when services or risk change, and invoicing through OpenInvoice.

sources.title: Prospective Suppliers
sources.supports: A producer qualifies contractors for health, safety and environment through ISNetworld before work; registration and qualification do not imply an award.

assumptions: Loaded costs are the organisation file's (base wage x 1.35 for benefits, payroll taxes, WCB and overhead).

The organisation file lists only the producer as the trigger and the producer as the receiver; the award is also handed to cs-msa-and-pricing-agreement and fo-frac-program-planning, and the prequalification record from hs-customer-safety-prequalification is an input.
The fracturing operations manager and the HSE data coordinator take small parts in the process although the process map does not list them.
The producer's evaluation period is modelled as one external wait; best and final rounds loop back through approval and upload.
No public source on Canadian oilfield tender cycle times was found; step times, waits, branch shares and the cycle time benchmark are tier C.
